blocks.t: **Objetivo de comunicação (C2):** eu consigo ler, ouvir, falar e escrever sobre oratória e discurso público a partir de uma biografia, analisando como a história de vida explica a força de um orador.

body: Esta aula treina **responder em frases completas (IELTS Speaking, TOEFL Speaking)**.

blocks.t: Toque em 🔊, ouça e repita cada palavra. Depois tente adivinhar o sentido.

blocks.name: Frederick Douglass (c. 1818–1895)
paras: Frederick Douglass was born into slavery in Maryland and **taught himself to read**, an act he later described as the first step toward freedom. In 1838 he **escaped** to the North and became, within a few years, one of the most **sought-after** anti-slavery speakers in the United States. His 1845 **Narrative** **bore witness** to slavery with a **restraint** that made it **all the more damning**.

His address of July 5, 1852, delivered in Rochester, New York, is **widely regarded** as a **masterpiece of irony**: **praising** the Founders, he **turned** the Fourth of July into **an indictment**. After the Civil War he **held** several federal posts and **kept speaking** on civil rights until his death in 1895.

items.q: The 1852 speech simply celebrated the Founders.
items.why: turned the Fourth of July into an indictment.

items.q: He stopped speaking after the Civil War.

blocks.body: Uma boa biografia mistura **fatos datados** (pretérito) e **avaliação** (*is widely regarded as*, *is often cited*). *All the more + adjetivo* realça uma consequência.
Atribua juízos de valor: *is widely regarded as* ✓, em vez de afirmar *is the best* ✗.

items.s: The speech is ___ regarded as a masterpiece of irony. (widely)
The restraint made it all the ___ damning. (more)

items.ans: Why is the 1852 speech so celebrated
items.pt: Por que o discurso de 1852 é tão celebrado?

body: **Bear witness to.** — Testemunhar.
**Speak truth to power.** — Dizer a verdade ao poder.
**Rise to the occasion.** — Estar à altura do momento.
**A voice in the wilderness.** — Voz que clama no deserto.
**Strike a chord.** — Tocar um ponto sensível.
**Hold the floor.** — Manter a palavra.
**Make history.** — Entrar para a história.
**Against all odds.** — Contra tudo e contra todos.
**Stand one’s ground.** — Manter-se firme.
**Set the tone.** — Dar o tom.
**Why is the 1852 speech so celebrated?** — Por que o discurso de 1852 é tão celebrado?
**Then let us read it aloud.** — Então vamos lê-lo em voz alta.
**Because he turned a holiday into an indictment?** — Porque transformou um feriado em acusação?

prompts.q: Summarize a life in two sentences.
prompts.model: Born into slavery, he taught himself to read and became a leading orator.
The speech is widely regarded as a masterpiece.
Her calm made the accusation all the more powerful.

blocks.task: Write a 6-sentence biographical paragraph about a public speaker you admire, using a relative clause, an appositive and all the more.
blocks.model: Wangari Maathai, a Kenyan environmentalist and Nobel laureate, founded the Green Belt Movement in 1977. She taught rural women to plant trees, an act that linked ecology to dignity. Her speeches, which were plain and patient, made her demands all the more persuasive. She is widely regarded as a pioneer of community-led conservation. She kept campaigning despite arrests and threats. Her legacy lives in millions of trees.

body: Treine esta habilidade com o formato de tarefas curtas das provas (TOEFL/IELTS).
Leia o enunciado primeiro e procure as palavras-chave.
Use exemplos reais da vida dos alunos e peça frases próprias.
Corrija o erro mais frequente da aula em grupo, sem expor o aluno.
Retome o conteúdo na aula seguinte com um exercício curto.
